text:
When I am dead, my dearest,

sing no sad songs for me;

plant no roses at my head

nor shadowy cypress tree:

be the green grass above me,

wet with showers and dewdrops;

and if you will, remember,

and if you will, forget.


I shall not see the shadows,

I shall not feel the rain,

I shall not hear the nightingale

singing its pain:

and dreaming through a twilight

that does not rise or set,

happily I may remember,

and happily I may forget.




"When I am Dead, My Dearest"

translation.title: When I Am Dead, My Dearest
translation.editorial_note: The translation follows Rossetti's quiet permission to mourn gently, remember, or forget.
